svg.text: F-193 to F-213: which term each coder says is wrong (red = held, blue = judged, violet = both, grey = neither). Ringed: a side-split.
The 109 uses of “error” in the journals of Sessions 100–119: practice (upper) and fresh reader (lower).
Red = T, an error named against a value nobody holds; blue = N, against a held reference; amber = concept; light = register, name, other.
Practice: 0 T. Reader: 2 T (U084, U106) — both passages leave the reference’s holder unnamed. Reader B split 2 of 3 disagreements: S113.SIDE fires.
